dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (日医標準レセプトソフト); compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux; uses COPY with REPLACING, INDEXED files, no EXEC SQL/CICS
evidence: SELECT ... ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC
no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS
fixed-format source with Japanese EUC comments

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) file creation for monthly billing — generates receipt detail files (RECE01) and medical fee claim files (RECE01X) for national health insurance (社保/国保) processing
purpose.summary: ORCR0010 is a batch program in the JMA ORCA standard medical receipt software system. It creates and updates indexed receipt detail and medical fee claim files for monthly billing cycles, handling insurance combinations, local public expense (地方公費), mid-month insurance changes, and various prefecture-specific rules. It writes error records to an error file and calls multiple subprograms for data retrieval and processing.

notable_features: 38 COPY statements with REPLACING for copybook reuse
241 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
INDEXED file I/O with DYNAMIC access (RECE01-FILE, RECE01X-FILE)
Extensive Japanese EUC-encoded comments documenting revision history
No COMP-3 usage despite financial calculations
Long revision history spanning 2000–2011 with named developers
Prefecture-specific processing logic (Fukuoka, Hokkaido, Tokyo, Niigata, etc.)
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments are actually EUC-JP encoded Japanese text (garbled in latin-1 view). Source is clearly the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system. The 53 lines over 72 characters are within normal fixed-format COBOL tolerance (indicator/continuation area usage). No COMP-3 is unusual for financial data but consistent with ORCA's style using PIC 9 fields.
